newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Yen, Swiss franc dominate Hungary FX futures mkt.
newsitem.headline: Yen, Swiss franc dominate Hungary FX futures mkt.

text.p: Yen futures were the most popular for the fourth consecutive day on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE)'s forex futures market, dealers said on Wednesday.
The yen and the Swiss franc accounted for two-thirds of the BCE's turnover of 5.6 billion forints, with 16,950 and 7,510 contracts respectively.
"The yen reached such lows against the dollar that traders are banking on a possible intervention or at least an imminent correction," said Janos Szolyka of Swap.

December yen was the most traded maturity with a turnover of 13,770 contracts. It rose a marginal two fillers to 161.62 forints against 100 yens. September yen went down 30 fillers to 154.70 while March eased 55 fillers to 166.45.
December was also the favourite month for the Swiss franc with 7,100 contracts. It finished at 136.50, up 0.10.

The usually illiquid sterling market had a relatively large turnover of 3,230 contracts and it rose 60 fillers for June to 299.30 forints, 3.9 forints for September to 309.70 and 2.1 forints for December to 316.
"The sterling is quite strong at the moment and fundamentals of the British industry are also good. Elections are the only uncertainty factor," Szolyka said.
The Budapest Stock Exchange saw a very thin currency futures turnover of 35 contracts or 51.7 million forints, almost equally divided between December mark and September dollar.
The mark eased 19 fillers for December to 116.2 forints while the dollar rose 34 fillers for December to finish at 190.28.
The BSE trades in marks, dollars and Ecus.
